subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: What should Telegram do when a voice update's Telegram source timestamp is far older than dispatch time and the resulting direct-message run aborts before a visible reply?
rationale: Source inspection shows plausible gaps, but the safe threshold, restart/alert behavior, and user-visible fallback text are product choices that affect real Telegram transport behavior.

options.title: Define minimal latency and fallback policy
options.body: Choose a source-age threshold, diagnostic fields, restart or alert behavior, and direct-message failure text before queuing a repair.

options.title: Split the remaining work across existing trackers
options.body: Route the general delay part to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78079 and the voice recovery reply part to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91652 if maintainers decide this combined issue should not stay canonical.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue in live-repro state until a Telegram proof captures the exact source timestamp, dispatch timestamp, abort reason, and delivery outcome on current main.

recommendation.title: Define minimal latency and fallback policy
recommendation.body: Choose a source-age threshold, diagnostic fields, restart or alert behavior, and direct-message failure text before queuing a repair.

likelyOwner.reason: The policy choice spans Telegram liveness and visible fallback semantics, and steipete has prior history splitting the polling liveness surface plus broad adjacent ownership signal.
